newsitem.title: USA: N.Y.C to sell $500 mln new money bonds in November.
newsitem.headline: N.Y.C to sell $500 mln new money bonds in November.

text.p: New York City on Wednesday said that it planned to sell during the week of November 4 approximately $400 million of tax-exempt bonds and $100 million of taxable issues for its capital program.

A New York City official added that depending upon market conditions, the city also might include a refunding in the November offering, selling approximately $440 million of tax-exempt issues and $60 million of taxable debt.

Bear Stearns Cos Inc's Bear, Stearns & Co was selected to senior manage the syndicate, which also includes Lehman Brothers, Merrill Lynch, Prudential Securities and Smith Barney, for the tax-exempt offerings.
However, the city has yet to finalize how the taxable sales will be handled or what type of debt will be issued.

Whether the debt will be sold overseas, as it was in late June, when the city took its first plunge in Europe's debt markets by selling a $180 million Eurobond in London, has yet to be decided, the city official said.
New York City estimated it saved $500,000 in borrowing costs because Europeans were willing to pay higher prices.
In 1993, the city tested overseas debt markets for the first time when it sold a $200 million yen-denominated issue, called a "Samurai" bond, which was linked to a currency swap.

New York City also has not determined whether the new debt that will be offered in November will be sold competively or through negotiation. "We will make a subsequent announcement," the city official said, declining further comment on the issue. The city first had planned to sell the bonds around the end of October, and the official said that the slight delay was not significant.
